1.
The petition U/s 166 and 140 of

Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 was filed on 04.08.2021 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.70,00,000/- (Rupees Seventy Lac Only) in respect of the death of one Sh. Sumeet Singh @ Hunny S/o Late Sh. Gurdev Singh (hereinafter referred to as "deceased")
due to a motor vehicular accident dated 02.03.2021 at about 01.30 PM at Vandemataram Road Opposite 24x7 towards Patel Nagar, Delhi involving a vehicle bearing registration no. HR-13H-9275 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle').
A Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on MACT No. 590/2021 Sukh Pal & Ors.
Vs. Maninder Singh & Anr.
Pages No. 4/16 PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

Date:
2025.08.05 14:54:31 +0530 02.12.2021(which was registered on 06.12.2021) by the Investigating Officer.

As per DAR, at the relevant date and time, a scooter no. DL-8SQ-9570 was hit by a white colour Santro Car No.
HR-13H-9275 and deceased was admitted in Dr. RML Hospital vide MLC No.E-43449/21 and declared brought dead by the doctors.
An FIR no. 34/2021, PS Rajinder Nagar, U/s 279/337/304A IPC was registered.
Petitioner no.1 & 2 are sisters of the deceased.
R-1 is stated to be the driver and R-2 is owner of the offending vehicle.
This Tribunal directed the respondents to file written statements in response to the said petition.
2. However, no written statement was filed on behalf of R-1 & R-2.
Therefore, they were proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 28.03.2024.
PETITIONER'S EVIDENCE 3.
In support of contentions, the petitioners examined one witness i.e. petitioner no. 2 as PW-1.
PW-1 Ms. Neetu Rahi D/o Late Sh. Gurdev Singh deposed that she is the LRs of deceased Sukhpal who was mother of deceased and her deceased brother died in the road accident.

ARGUMENTS 4.
Oral submissions were advanced on behalf of petitioners.
5. I have perused the entire record and given due consideration on the submissions made.
COMPENSATION 6.

The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the following heads:-
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY
7. In this regard, it is claimed that at the relevant time, the deceased was working as a sales staff and earning Rs.25,000/- per MACT No. 590/2021 Sukh Pal & Ors.
Vs. Maninder Singh & Anr.
Pages No.

6/16 PANKAJ SHARMA Date:
SHARMA 2025.08.05 14:54:35 +0530 month.
However, petitioners have not placed any documentary proof in respect to employment and earnings of the deceased.
Petitioners have filed job certificate Ex. PW-1/6 of deceased.

As per the same,
deceased was earning Rs.850/- per day.
Accordingly, the monthly salary of the deceased was Rs.25,500/- at the time of accident.
7.1 Petitioners have placed on record the copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased, as per which the age of deceased was 32 years.
Therefore, the age of deceased was 32 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

sentences.text:
SLP (Civil)
No. 25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017, the multiplier of '16' is held applicable for calculating the loss of dependency caused to the petitioners on account of death of the deceased.

7.2 Coming to the dependency of deceased at the time of accident, it may be observed that the deceased was survived by his two sisters and mother (now deceased) as he was working and taking care of his family consisting of his two sisters.
7.3 Irrespective of this, one half of the earnings of deceased MACT No. 590/2021 Sukh Pal & Ors.
Vs. Maninder Singh & Anr.
Pages No. 7/16

5
SHARMA 2025.08.05 14:54:37 +0530 shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses in view of the law already discussed above.
Further, since this Tribunal has assumed that the age of deceased was 32 years at the time of accident, in view of the law laid down in the case of Pranay Sethi & Ors.
(Supra), the petitioner is also held entitled to an addition of 50% of the above amount of his earnings towards future prospects.
7.4 Thus, the loss of dependency qua the deceased in the present case comes to Rs.36,72,000/- (rounded off) (Rs.25,500/- X 1/2 X 150/100 X 16 X 12).
This amount is awarded to the petitioners under this head.
(ii) COMPENSATION UNDER NON-PECUNIARY HEADS 8.
In terms of propositions laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajwati @ Rajjo & Ors.

Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Civil Appeal No. 8179/2022 decided on 09/12/2022, the petitioners are also held entitled to amounts of Rs.20,000/- each under the heads of loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Further, in view of subsequent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd Vs Satinder Kaur & Ors MANU/HC/0500/2020 and The New India Assurance Company Ltd & Ors Vs Somwati & Ors MANU/HC/0674/2020, the petitioners are also entitled to compensation under the head "loss of consortium": -

Out of the awarded amount, petitioner no. 2 Neetu Rahi is awarded a sum of Rs.45,00,000/- (Rupees Fourty Five Lac Only) and the said amount is directed to be kept with State Bank of India, Branch Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi in MACAD in the form of 225 monthly fixed deposit receipts (FDRs) payable in equal amounts for a period of 1 to 225 months in succession, as per the scheme formulated by Central Motor Vehicles (fifth Amendment) Rules, 2022 [(Directions at serial no. 35, 36 of Procedure for Investigation of Motor Vehicle Accidents (under Rule 150A)].
The remaining amount of Rs.5,86,400/- (Rupees Five Lac Eighty Six Thousand Four Hundred only)
is also directed to be released into her above said account, which can be withdrawn and utilized by the petitioner Neetu Rahi.
